newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian money market inactive as Bombay banks shut.
newsitem.headline: Indian money market inactive as Bombay banks shut.

text.p: India's inter-bank call money and securities markets were largely inactive on Friday as banks in Bombay, the commercial capital, were closed for a holiday, dealers said.

Securities prices reacted sharply on Thursday after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Wednesday set a yield of 11.83 percent against market expectations of 11.90-11.95 percent, at a 30 billion rupee auction of six-year bonds.
Prices rose for securities of all maturities as bonds were repriced after Wednesday's auction of six-year bonds. Most of the action was in bonds with tenors up to 2004.
Dealers said they expected call money to trade between 2.0 percent and 3.0 percent, when markets resume on Saturday.
